title: Hand-Built BXT Gravel Bike | 6 Months / 2,000km Update | Sensah SRX Groupset & Elitewheels ENT.

takeaways.text: After about 2,000 km including single track there were no cracks, creaks or loosening; the only issues were a clicking bottom bracket (replaced with a SRAM one) and a squealing front rotor.
Schwalbe G-One Bite 45 mm tires leave loads of room; she believes 50 mm would fit, against the 47 mm frame specification, but has not tried it.
The whole build cost about £1,350 (September 2025); DPD delivery of the frame with prepaid duties was about £70 and took roughly a month.
Her size-52 build weighs about 9 kg.
She runs 140 mm rotors; the fork takes 160 mm, but the rear is tight with TRP calipers and the frame is not specified for 160 mm.
At 57–58 kg she finds it comfortable and responsive with a little flex that she does not mind; her husband found the same bike jarring, which she cites as proof that ride feel is personal.

disclosure: The owner built the bike with her own parts; the only affiliate link is to an unrelated clothing brand.
summary: Six-month, 2,000 km owner update on a size-52 BXT Gravel 135 built with a SENSAH SRX Pro 1× groupset; not the candidate's GRX complete build.
